exact_excerpts.text: Effect: This property provides an enhancement bonus to confirm critical hits and critical hit damage. A +10 Seeker item adds +10 to your confirm critical roll and +10 damage to your critical damage (before multipliers). The additional damage only applies if you actually score critical damage. If your target negates the critical hit, for example by fortification, extra seeker damage does not apply. Seeker affects all your attacks (single weapon melee, dual weapon melee, and ranged). For example, if you are using two weapons, only one needs to have seeker but both benefit from it. Or you can place seeker on an accessory. The same is true of Backstabbing, Doublestrike, and Stunning. Seeker items can provide various types of bonus. Regular Seeker grants Enhancement bonus, then there's Insightful Seeker and much rarer Quality Seeker. The former Exceptional Seeker grants Insight bonus. See also Accuracy and Deadly
exact_excerpts.completeness: Complete displayed Effect prose, including the final See also link labels. The original last link label had no exposed final punctuation, so none is added.

following_list: Essence Crafting: prefix Seeker (up to +15) and extra Insightful Seeker (up to +7)
exact_excerpts.completeness: Complete four-entry Notes list. The large preceding Found on item-category catalogue is deliberately omitted. The listed crafting sources were not opened or newly verified.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Critical confirmation and extra damage
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The +10 example grants +10 to the critical-confirmation roll and +10 critical damage before multipliers. Confirmation and damage are separate effects in the paragraph.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: The source does not provide a full critical-confirmation hit formula, a natural-roll rule, a critical-threat-range increase or a numeric increase in critical multiplier. Seeker's pre-multiplier damage bonus is not itself an extra multiplier step.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Interaction with the critical multiplier
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The article explicitly places Seeker damage before multipliers. If S is an applicable Seeker damage bonus and M is the applicable critical damage multiplier, its pre-other-modifier contribution under that multiplier is S × M; the source's +10 example would therefore contribute 10 × M.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: This is algebraic application of the stated placement, not a verbatim worked multiplication example. The article does not determine a weapon's or build's final M, certify that every critical-multiplier source stacks, or supply a Ranged Power factor or full damage-processing order.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Fortification and other critical negation
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: Extra Seeker damage applies only when actual critical damage is scored. If the target negates the critical, with fortification given as an example, extra Seeker damage does not apply.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: The page does not establish the complete fortification check order, bypass calculation or a particular target's immunity. No amount of Seeker is treated as fortification bypass merely because it improves confirmation.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Attack and equipment scope
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: Explicit general applicability and equipment examples
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: Seeker affects single-weapon melee, dual-weapon melee and ranged attacks. With two weapons, only one needs Seeker for both to benefit; an accessory can also provide it.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: This establishes attack coverage and the stated one-source applicability, not positive accumulation of multiple Seeker items or an interaction with Ranged Power. No item or weapon was selected.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Bonus typing and stacking
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: Explicit regular/legacy typing and variant distinctions; broad stacking rule absent
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: Regular Seeker explicitly grants Enhancement. The former Exceptional Seeker explicitly grants Insight. The same paragraph says Seeker items provide various bonus types and names Insightful Seeker and Quality Seeker variants.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: The paragraph does not explicitly state a universal positive stacking rule for all these variants or all mixed bonus types. The variant names are retained as written rather than used to invent a new standalone type-definition sentence or a certified summed Seeker total. No duplicate-item stacking rule is inferred from the dual-weapon example.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Ranged Power
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: Ranged attack applicability explicit; Ranged Power scaling not explicitly established by this own-page text
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The article explicitly includes ranged attacks, but does not name Ranged Power or state its coefficient for Seeker damage.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: No scaling interaction is certified from the word ranged alone. This is a bounded evidence gap, not proof that Seeker is excluded from Ranged Power. The separate Melee Power article's broad straight-weapon-damage wording does not itself explicitly classify Seeker's conditional bonus for an RP calculation.

exact_excerpts.text: Melee Power, introduced in Update 23, is similar in effect to Spell Power and increases straight weapon damage in addition to certain static effects from enhancements. It can be gained from certain feats, enhancements, melee epic destinies, items and spells.
following_list: Melee Power is not applied to static damage riders like a sword's fire damage enchantment, but can apply to some Imbues.
Sneak Attack damage benefits even more from melee power, at 150% effectiveness.
exact_excerpts.completeness: Complete opening Overview paragraph and both applicability bullets.

exact_excerpts.text: The melee power rating provides a percentage adjustment to straight damage identical to that for ranged power (refer to following chart):
exact_excerpts.context: This explicit general relation immediately precedes the positive and negative formula bullets. The ranged power phrase is a link label.

formula_and_example_blocks.source_structure: Two top-level formula bullets, each with nested example or explanation bullets. This is not a source table.

blocks.exact_formula_statement: Positive ratings use the formula: Damage * (100 + Rating / 100)
exact_nested_entries: For example, a character with 20 melee power that rolls 50 damage with a melee weapon will actually deal a total of 50 * 1.2 = 60 damage

blocks.exact_formula_statement: Negative ratings use a different formula: Damage * 100 / (100 - Rating)
exact_nested_entries: This is more favorable than the positive rating formula would be for negative ratings
-50 rating means a character deals 100 / (100 - -50) = 100 / (100+50) = 100/150, or 2/3, or 66% damage

following_graph.note: The adjacent graph was exposed as an image link without its numeric contents. No values or corrected formula are inferred from an unseen graph.

formula_and_example_blocks.completeness: Complete positive/negative textual formula blocks and nested examples, preserving parentheses and the displayed 66% wording.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Straight weapon damage and exclusions
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: Melee Power increases straight weapon damage and certain static enhancement effects. The page excludes static riders such as a sword's fire enchantment, allows some Imbues, and states 150% effectiveness for Sneak Attack.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: Certain and some remain limiting terms. The page is not used to make every rider, spell, imbue or enhancement scale with Melee Power, or to infer an unlisted coefficient. The special-attack catalogue does not itself certify current tree access or every interaction.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Explicit general relation to Ranged Power
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: Direct equivalence for percentage adjustment to straight damage
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The Overview explicitly states that the percentage adjustment to straight damage is identical for melee power and ranged power.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: The sentence's scope is the percentage adjustment to straight damage. It does not automatically make every melee-specific rider, special-attack list, enhancement source or bonus-stacking relationship apply to ranged attacks. It also does not resolve the positive-formula inconsistency.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Positive formula versus worked example
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The printed expression is Damage * (100 + Rating / 100), while the worked example uses 50 * 1.2 = 60 at Rating 20. Under ordinary arithmetic precedence, the printed expression at those inputs gives 50 * (100 + 20 / 100) = 50 * 100.2 = 5010, not 60.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: The literal formula and worked example are both preserved. No parentheses are silently relocated, no corrected general formula is supplied from memory, and no entire rating curve is certified solely from a single worked point. The worked example directly supports its own 20-power, 50-to-60 statement.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Negative formula and examples
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: Direct formula with consistent fractional examples and source rounding
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The negative formula is Damage * 100 / (100 - Rating). At -50 it yields a factor of 100/150 = 2/3; at -100 it yields 1/2. The source displays 66% for the former and 50% for the latter.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: The 66% label is preserved as the article's approximation; 2/3 is approximately 66.67%, not exactly 66%. No new negative-rating source, floor, cap or damage-order rule is inferred.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Seeker and Ranged Power interaction
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: Not resolved by these two articles alone
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: Seeker explicitly contributes before critical multipliers and applies to ranged attacks. Melee Power describes straight weapon damage and its general percentage equivalence to Ranged Power, but neither captured text explicitly classifies the conditional Seeker damage as a specific RP-scaled component or states its RP coefficient.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: No S × M × RP-factor expression is certified here. Missing explicit classification or coefficient is treated as unverified, not as proof that Seeker does not scale. An applicable independently retained rule may resolve the relationship without requiring a pairwise sentence.

interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.subject: Bonus sources versus positive mixed-type stacking
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.status: No applicable general stacking rule captured
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.finding: The Overview names sources of Melee Power, while this focused receipt excludes the long source catalogue. A source list is not a positive general rule that every type or effect stacks.
interpretations_and_conditional_applicat.limits: No mixed Melee/Ranged Power total, final critical profile or selected build damage is certified by component truth alone.

synthesis.scope: Three normal articles only: Seeker, Melee Power, Overwhelming Critical. No linked critical-multiplier article, source tree, item or retained Ranged Power page was opened.

findings.explicit_rules: A +10 Seeker item adds +10 to the confirm-critical roll and +10 to critical damage before multipliers. Additional damage applies only when critical damage is actually scored. If the target negates the critical hit, for example through fortification, the extra Seeker damage does not apply. Seeker affects single-weapon melee, dual-weapon melee and ranged attacks; one weapon's Seeker can benefit both weapons and an accessory can supply it.
findings.conditional_arithmetic: For a confirmed, non-negated critical to which a critical multiplier M applies, an applicable Seeker damage component S included before that multiplier contributes S × M at that multiplication stage. Thus the stated +10 example would contribute 30 at a ×3 critical stage, before separately applicable other modifiers. This is arithmetic application of the premultiplier statement, not a worked example quoted from the article.
findings.limits: No critical-threat expansion, automatic confirmation or fortification bypass is conferred by this text. If the critical is negated, the extra Seeker damage is zero. The page does not establish that a specific target can be critically hit or certify the guide's final multiplier.

findings.explicit_rules: Seeker identifies regular Seeker as Enhancement, names Insightful and Quality Seeker variants, and explicitly says former Exceptional Seeker grants Insight. It expressly includes ranged attacks.
findings.limits: Naming multiple variants is not itself an explicit positive stacking rule for every combination. Seeker does not name Ranged Power or a specific RP scaling coefficient. Melee Power's straight-damage rule and its same-percentage-adjustment statement for RP are retained below, but do not explicitly classify Seeker's added critical damage for RP scaling. No Seeker × critical multiplier × RP formula is certified by this bounded set. Absence of such wording is not proof that RP does not scale Seeker.

findings.exact_positive_example: For example, a character with 20 melee power that rolls 50 damage with a melee weapon will actually deal a total of 50 * 1.2 = 60 damage
findings.analysis: With ordinary arithmetic precedence, the printed expression at Damage=50 and Rating=20 evaluates to 50 × (100 + 20/100) = 5010, while the explicit worked example gives 60. The discrepancy is in the observed source. The example directly supports the 1.2 factor at rating 20; a corrected general positive formula is not silently substituted or asserted as an exact quotation.
exact_negative_examples: -50 rating means a character deals 100 / (100 - -50) = 100 / (100+50) = 100/150, or 2/3, or 66% damage
findings.negative_example_note: The 66% wording is the source's rounded/truncated expression of 2/3; its exact fraction is preserved. No silent replacement with 66.666...% is made inside the quotation.
findings.retained_comparison: The capture reports Ranged Power675695 has the same positive-expression problem and a 20 RP example taking 100 damage to 120. That retained article was not reread. The new Melee Power observation repeats the conflict rather than resolving it independently.

sources: Special attacks affected by Melee Power
findings.explicit_rules: Melee Power increases straight weapon damage plus certain static effects from enhancements. It does not apply to static damage riders such as a sword's fire-damage enchantment, but can apply to some imbues. Sneak Attack is listed at 150% effectiveness. The article explicitly says its percentage adjustment to straight damage is identical to that for ranged power.
findings.limits: The explicit general relationship covers the percentage adjustment, not an assertion that all MP grants, source lists, special-attack coefficients or melee-only effects also grant or use RP. The catalogue of some special attacks is retained as article observations without a tree revisit. No universal all-damage scaling or new mixed-type RP stacking rule is supplied. The positive formula conflict remains visible.

findings.exact_general_rule: All effects that increase critical damage multiplier on rolls of 19-20 stack.
findings.explicit_component_context: Overwhelming Critical increases the critical damage multiplier by +1 when rolling 19 or 20 on an attack with any weapons used by the character. Notes also state that it functions with handwraps and shields.
findings.applicable_general_rule: This is positive general stacking evidence for effects whose documented scope meets the stated 19–20 multiplier condition. It can support combinations across feat, destiny, enhancement or weapon sources without requiring an exact pairwise sentence naming each source. The quoted rule contains no source-category exclusion.
findings.conditional_arithmetic: Given an established baseline critical multiplier and separately established simultaneously applicable +1 increases covered by this rule, those increases can be added on the qualifying 19/20 results. This arithmetic does not supply missing component values or activation conditions.
findings.limits: The rule is not a complete mixed critical-profile calculation. Each component still needs its documented value, weapon/stance/level/activation conditions and applicable roll scope. It does not by itself expand threat range, guarantee a critical hit, bypass confirmation or fortification, or establish every other multiplier/range interaction on other rolls. The linked Critical hit multiplier article was observed but not opened.

synthesis.useful_resolution: The formerly missing 19–20 multiplier stacking relationship has an explicit applicable general rule in Overwhelming Critical. The positive power-formula discrepancy remains unresolved by the new Melee Power source.
remaining_gaps: A non-conflicting exact general positive power formula in the captured source text; the worked 20-power example is clear but the printed formula disagrees.
Explicit classification/scaling of Seeker's additional critical damage by Ranged Power.
A broad positive rule for every intended mixed-type Seeker combination, if not supplied by separate retained bonus-type rules.
Final selected-build critical profile, including all independently established component conditions, threat-range and non-19/20 interactions.
